description: GDIS is a geocoded extension of natural disasters in the EM-DAT Emergency Events Database, giving 39,953 locations for 9,924 disasters worldwide from 1960 to 2018. It covers floods, storms, earthquakes, landslides, droughts, volcanic activity and extreme temperatures recorded in EM-DAT that could be geocoded, linking each disaster number to administrative units of the GADM 2018 boundaries, mostly at level 1 (state or province) and at best level 3 (district or village). It was created by Rosvold and Buhaug and is distributed by NASA's Socioeconomic Data and Applications Center at CIESIN, Columbia University, now through NASA Earthdata. Coverage is global. Format and access: GIS files through Earthdata Search with a codebook PDF; the NASA metadata was read, the SEDAC page itself blocked scripts. Licence: SEDAC terms, not read; free. Caveats: locations are administrative areas, not hazard footprints, disasters that could not be geocoded are missing, and impacts must be joined from EM-DAT under its own terms. It lets EM-DAT losses be mapped for hazard exposure and resilience studies of infrastructure regions. Related catalogue records are EM-DAT and the global single- and multi-hazard events dataset built from both.
